_readme: What the community theme registry is expected to be serving for each theme this app ALSO bundles.
Three of the themes in this folder exist twice: here, and in the registry at the url below, so the
Appearance panel can send users somewhere to browse and download them. Nothing used to notice when a
bundled theme gained a view and its registry twin did not, and both had quietly rotted (issue #57):
the registry's Channels had no nowplayingAudio view, a grid instead of the channels browse layout and
no detail actionrow, and its Triple had nothing but `home` — downloading either gave you a strictly
worse theme than the one already in the app, under the same name.
canonicalSha256 is the hash of the theme's MEANING, not its bytes: parse the theme.json, re-serialise
it with sorted keys and no whitespace, hash that. So a reformat is not drift and the two repos are free
to spell the same theme differently. native/tools/theme-registry-sync.py computes it; the headless probe
suite runs that script with --check on every push.
TO CHANGE A PUBLISHED THEME:
1. edit it here, as usual;
2. the gate goes red, naming the theme;
3. run  native/tools/theme-registry-sync.py --update --assume-published "<why>"  and commit the
refreshed record with the theme change. "<why>" is normally just "published on merge": at that
moment the copy genuinely has not happened, and saying so is the honest state (see below);
4. on merge to main, the publish job does the copy and rewrites step 3's claim with a real sha.
There is no step where you copy anything into the registry by hand. On a push to main that touches
native/themes2/**, .github/workflows/publish-themes.yml checks the registry out with a deploy key,
runs --publish (which copies exactly the targets listed below and nothing else), pushes, then reruns
--update --registry-commit <the sha it just pushed>, commits THAT back to this repo, and finally
re-fetches what the registry serves to confirm it matches. verify-registry.yml re-checks the same
thing every Monday, which catches what the publisher cannot see: a direct edit there, a revert, or a
publish that never ran.
publishedAgainst is the receipt (issue #151). --update recomputes these hashes from the BUNDLED themes
and has never once looked at the registry, so before #151 a record refreshed WITHOUT the copy was
byte-indistinguishable from one refreshed after it. That is not a hypothetical: #57 and #32 both ran
the refresh alone, so this file asserted the registry was current while it still served the pre-#29
Triple — `home` and nothing else — and the gate was green over it for days.
So the record has to name what it was published against, and there are exactly two things it may say:
* registryCommit — the sha in the registry those copies were pushed as. Unverifiable in the offline
probe suite, deliberately, but falsifiable from anywhere with a network call:
native/tools/theme-registry-sync.py --verify-registry
This is now normally MACHINE-written: the publish job sets it from the commit it actually created,
so the claim substantiates itself instead of resting on somebody remembering to type it.
* unverifiedReason — no publish has happened, and here is why. Written by  --update
--assume-published "<why>", and printed by the gate on every run. It is the correct state for a
branch that edits a theme, and the publish job replaces it the moment the merge lands.
A bare --update is refused. The gate still cannot PROVE the registry is current — nothing in an offline
suite can — but it no longer silently implies it either, and it is no longer the only thing trying to.
Adding a NEW theme here is still a two-repo change: --publish refuses to CREATE a path the registry
does not already carry, because index.json needs a `description` that exists nowhere in theme.json and
a theme folder nothing lists is a theme nobody can find. Make the registry side first.
The registry ALSO serves four themes that are not bundled here (Default, Grid, Lumen, Midnight), which
this file cannot see at all. Their check is native/tools/theme-registry-validate.py, run over there.

publishedAgainst.unverifiedReason: THEME_FORMAT.md: document the lyrics element (issue #142); publishes with the themed lyric panel on merge
